steps: Plan, frame & protect
Frame to the minimums (55" enclosure width, 41" height, 20" depth) with room for gas and electrical on the left; settle the hearth pad and finishing-guide kit before the unit goes in.

Before installing, decide the location, vent configuration, gas piping, wiring, framing and finish details, hearth pad and any accessories.

  • Framing minimums: 55" enclosure width, 48" finished width, 41" height, 20" depth; 72" from unit base to room ceiling.
  • Indoors only, protected from precipitation and moisture, with ambient temperature between 32°F and 110°F.
  • Set it on wood, masonry or metal extending the full width and depth of the fireplace, never directly on carpeting or vinyl.
  • Build the chase like an outside wall: insulate walls, ceiling, base plate and cantilever floor; vapor and air barriers per regional code; caulk fire stops with high temperature caulk. On a cement slab, plywood under the unit stops cold conducting up.
  • Finishing guides: the standard guide suits inside-finish fronts; doors need a faceplate. Grace, Mission and Willowbrook fronts need the Flush Mount or Recessed Mount guide kit, so choose the wall finish first. Guides protrude 1"; factory guides are riveted (remove with a ⅛" drill bit).
Note: p. 30 says the Recessed Mount guide kit is required when wall finish exceeds 2 ½" in depth, and also that the Flush Mount guide kit only needs finish less than 3" thick including backing.
Unpack & set the firebox
Open and check the manual packet, unbolt the unit from the pallet and bend up the shipping clips; set it in the chase, level and plumb, and secure it to the framing studs.

Manual packet (white box), all to stay with the homeowner: glass latch tool # HA-77-00256, remote # HA-110-00105 with 3 AAA batteries, backup battery holder # 05-02-00345 with 4 AA batteries, backup power harness # 10-03-00128 and the owner's manual. Log set, firebox liner and decorative front are bought separately.

  • Net weight 300 lbs.: team lift. The four lifting handles (one each side, two on the rear wall) are for lifting and short moves only; don't carry it by the handles alone.
  • Unbolt from the pallet, bend up the shipping clips, place in the framed chase, level and plumb, secure to the framing studs.
  • Manufactured (mobile) home: bolt the unit to the floor and ground it.
  • The accent light bulb (G9 xenon, 25W) and lens come installed.
LP conversion (if burning LP)
Fit kit # HA-110-00084: #54 orifices front and rear, pilot clip to LP, motorized LP regulator, and the filled-in LP label. Best done before the unit goes into its cavity.

Kit # HA-110-00084 holds a motorized LP pressure regulator # 907.012, two #54 orifices (# 65-14-00054), an L-shaped Torx wrench and the LP conversion label. A qualified service agency must install it.

  1. Remove the 3 burner screws (¼" hex driver) and lift out both burners; remove the 2 airbox screws and lift out the airbox.
  2. With a ½" deep well socket, holding the fitting with a wrench, replace the front and rear orifices with #54.
  3. Grip the pilot base with vice grips, loosen its hex base ¼ turn with a 7/16" open end wrench, push the NAT/LP clip all the way in (no "NAT" visible) and retighten.
  4. Refit the airbox and burners: front burner parallel to the unit face, pilot hoods aimed at the flame propagation ports.
  5. Shut off gas and power. Through the left-side access panel, use Torx T20 to remove screws (A), tower (B) and spring/diaphragm (C); check gasket (D); fit the stepper motor regulator with the supplied M4 x 0.7 screws at 25 lb-in, plus or minus 5; apply label (G).
  6. Fill out and attach the LP conversion label.

Then confirm inlet and outlet pressures conform, the main burner lights immediately without lifting, and the pilot flames are at least 1" long and overlap the ports on both burners.
Install the vent system
5" x 8" coaxial rigid pipe, every joint twist-locked; 1" clearance at sides and bottom, 3" above horizontal runs; wall thimble through any combustible wall; cap right side up.

• Pre-assemble and measure the run before cutting. Fixed lengths are preferred over telescoping sections; never separate telescoping sections.
  • Openings: 10-3/4" x 10-3/4" in the wall (a 9-inch diameter hole is acceptable in non-combustible masonry), 10" x 10" in ceilings and roofs, with a fire stop spacer at each floor.
  • Minimum-rise horizontal: 9" vertical, one 90° elbow, 12" max horizontal. The elbow centerline is 46 ⅜" up from the fireplace floor level; mark the wall at 46-3/8" plus ¼" per foot of horizontal run.
  • Combustible wall thickness 4" to 8" maximum. Horizontal pipe ends flush with the exterior wall; the cap is not recessed, screwed tight to the wall and caulked.
  • Vertical: flashing sealed with roofing over its top edge, storm collar and cap, attic insulation shield, and the vent enclosed where it passes through occupied spaces above the first floor.

Vent cap location (from the cap center)

Above grade, veranda, porch, deck, balcony18 inches (45 cm) min.
Window or door that may be opened18 inches (45 cm) min.
Ventilated / unventilated soffit18" min.; 24" to vinyl soffit
Outside corner12 inches (30 cm)
Inside corner12 inches (30 cm); vinyl surfaces require 24" min
Service regulator vent outlet3 feet min.
Non-mechanical air supply inlet12 inches (30 cm) min.
Mechanical air supply inlet (USA)3 feet above, if within 10 feet horizontally
Above public paved sidewalk / driveway7 feet (2.1 m) min.
Under veranda, porch, deck, balcony18 inches (45 cm) min.
Vertical cap to any surface24" min. horizontal

Not above a meter/regulator assembly within 3 feet horizontally of its center-line (within a height of 15 feet). Use heat shield # AA-11-00458 where the exterior wall is vinyl, wood or other combustible material. Two gravity direct vent caps side by side: 18" min. between centerlines.

Massachusetts: sidewall terminations less than seven (7) feet above grade bring CO-detector and signage requirements (p. 9).
Gas supply & leak test
1/2" NPT female inlet, entering on the left; size the line from the table, drip leg recommended; leak-test every field and factory joint with a gas sniffer.

Size the line from the supply regulator to the factory manual shutoff valve:

0-10 ftSch. 40: 1/2" NG, 3/8" LP · Type L: 1/2" NG, 3/8" LP
10-40 ftSch. 40: 1/2" NG, 1/2" LP · Type L: 5/8" NG, 1/2" LP
40-100 ftSch. 40: 1/2" NG, 1/2" LP · Type L: 3/4" NG, 1/2" LP
100-150 ftSch. 40: 3/4" NG, 1/2" LP · Type L: 7/8" NG, 5/8" LP
150-200 ftSch. 40: 3/4" NG, 1/2" LP · Type L: 7/8" NG, 3/4" LP
  • Never plastic pipe. Use brass-to-brass fittings on CSST. Supply a ½" NPT male fitting to the 1/2" female inlet.
  • Add an external keyed manual shutoff if local code requires one. The factory shutoff sits in the left-side convection chamber (glass latch tool, 90° counterclockwise closes it).
  • Pressure-testing the supply piping: disconnect the appliance above 1/2 psi (3.5 kPa); isolate it by closing its shutoff at or below 1/2 psi.
  • Leak-test all field-installed joints and the factory gas train with soap and water solution or a gas sniffer, and check pressures before facing materials go on.
Verify orifices & input rate
Check the stamped orifice sizes (NG #38 rear / #44 front; LP #54 / #54), check manifold pressure (3.5" WC NG, 10.0" WC LP, +/- 1/8") and clock the gas meter on NG.

1. Read the size stamped on each main orifice body: NG #38 rear and #44 front, LP #54 rear and #54 front, for all elevations.
  2. Check that manifold pressure is within 3.5" WC +/- 1/8" (NG) or 10.0" WC +/- 1/8" (LP); the pressure taps are on the main gas valve.
  3. NG: note the meter reading, turn off all other appliances and their pilots, run 30 minutes on maximum flame, turn off burner and pilot, read the meter again.
  4. (Final − initial) therms × 100,000 × 2 must be at least the maximum input rate (44,000 Btu/Hr.).

High-altitude de-rating: fill in the High Altitude De-Rating Label from the owner's manual packet and attach it to the back of the listing label plate; LP conversion labels go on the same surface.
Electrical & backup DC inlet
Bring 120 VAC, hot at all times with no switch, to the left-side junction box; install the backup DC power inlet box up to 5 feet to the left.

1. Remove the junction box cover plate (two screws) and route the house power cable through its strain relief.
  2. Take the plug labeled TO HOUSE POWER from the manual packet; strip and join the color-coded wires with the supplied wire nuts (braided to braided: strip ½" and twist; braided to solid: strip the solid ½", the braid ¾", and wrap the braid around).
  3. Plug it into the plug toward the front of the fireplace at the back of the outlet box (keyed, so it can't go in wrong), tuck the wires in and refit the cover.

Ground per local codes, or NFPA 70 / CSA C22.1. Backup DC inlet: the 6-foot harness allows the single gang box up to 5 feet left of the unit, max 18" to the box center (or matching the room's outlets); don't staple the harness; fit a supplied cover plate (white or beige) and the DC inlet decal. Show the homeowner how to connect the DC battery pack.
Liner, logs & glass door
Install the firebox liner kit and the chosen log set (Norway spruce, white oak or birch) per their own instructions, then hang and latch the glass door centered in the opening.

The liner kit, the log set, coals and inswool media each follow the instructions packed with them. Give the log set instructions to the homeowner.

  • Logs or coals must never block the pilot flame or the main burner flame.
  • Door: set the two bottom tabs in the firebox slots, center left to right, rotate it in until the gasket touches, then hook both top spring latches with the glass latch tool.
  • Check the glass gasket every time the door comes off or goes back on: it is a 4-piece assembly and the corner joints must butt together. Gaps cause exhaust leaks and acrid smells.
Test fire: flame, shutters & damper
The pilot must light both burners immediately; the flame must be stable, not lifting, and cycle on/off without delay after 5 minutes. Then set the air shutters and fine-tune the vent damper.

• Fresh batteries in the remote; synchronize the remote and ignition module.
  • Pilot lights immediately and lights front and rear burners; flame runs promptly along the rear burner. Don't proceed unless the burner cycles on/off without delay and the flame is stable and not lifting after 5 minutes.
  • Flame lifting? Turn it off and check every vent joint is twist-locked and leak-proof and the cap is right side up.

Air shutters (p. 67)

The cables are in the air gap on the left side of the glass door frame: top cable = rear burner, bottom = front. Hook the ring with the glass latch tool; push to close, pull to open. Too blue: close in 1/8" increments. Soot on the glass: open fully and burn four to six hours, then close back in 1/8" increments. Try each setting approx. ½ hr. LP: a properly set shutter gives an approximate 2" high blue base. Above 4,500' some variation may be needed.

Note: the lighting checklist gives the natural gas air shutter opening as 0" to ⅛" (p. 66); the air shutter section says 1/8" open (p. 67). Both give ¼" to ½" for LP.

Vent damper (p. 63)

Rod above the glass frame, at the center of the convection chamber: hook the glass latch tool in its end, pull out about 1/8" and turn clockwise to close; a pointer shows the position. Judge the flames after 20 minutes. Horizontal terminations: never close it completely. Flames ghosting off the burners, or sooting on LP: open it fully and work back in increments.

Reference: after 30 minutes or longer at maximum, a normal rear flame is 1 to 2 inches above the rear log top edge.
Cure, then hand over
Run the 3-step curing cycle as the final install step, before finishing materials go on; then train the owner and complete the warranty registration.

Cure with the barrier screen on and the blowers running in step 1, so smoke doesn't stain the wall finish: Manual mode, Hi flame, fan level 3 for at least 2 hours, then cool; Hi with the fan off until odors diminish; then fan level 1. Expect smoke (it sets off smoke alarms). More than 10 continuous hours on high isn't unusual.

Hand-over (p. 87)

  • Leave the manual packet: owner's manuals, remote, glass latch tool, backup battery system.
  • Show how to remove and refit the decorative front and the glass door; explain the barrier screen requirement.
  • Remote: CPI and back to IPI (CPI suggested in the cold season), lighting, flame level, fan, accent light, rear burner, the three thermostat modes, lockout reset.
  • Backup battery use in an outage, the master switch and emergency shutoff, and the manual gas valve with the glass latch tool.
  • Tell the owner periodic maintenance is required; complete the warranty registration.

panels.title: Soot on the viewing glass
items: Burner air shutter closed too much → open it fully
Exhaust damper closed too much → open it
Glass door seal compromised → gasket corners can't bulge; white through the bulb and not sticking → replace
Incorrect gas pressure or orifice size → check orifices and outlet pressure (3.5" W.C. NG; 10" W.C. LP)

panels.title: Flame lifts off or lights late
items: Logs or coals blocking the pilot or main burner flame
Vent pipes not "twist locked" and leak-proof
Pilot flames not overlapping the burner propagation ports (1" min. long)

panels.title: Pilot slow to light or keeps sparking
items: More than 10 seconds to light → check pilot spark rod position and ignitor wires for pinched or damaged areas
Sparking continues 5 seconds after the pilot lights → dirty flame sensor; clean with emery cloth
Still sparking → check the flame sensor lead wire for damage or grounding

panels.title: Ghosting flames, lockouts, outages
items: Flames ghost off burners, or LP soot → open the vent damper fully, then close back in increments
"Low profile" vent caps → exhaust recirculation and ghosting flames
Pilot fails to light → lockout; turn off, wait 5 minutes, retry
Cold flue in winter → CPI increases startup draft and helps avoid lockout
Frequent pilot outages → diagnose the primary cause; don't assume the ignition control is faulty

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
This fireplace lights itself: an electronic igniter lights the pilot, and the pilot lights the burners. You start it with the remote. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Before you start

  • Smell all around the fireplace for gas, including down by the floor. Some gas is heavier than air and settles low.
  • Check that the master switch is on (up). The remote can't talk to the fireplace while it's off.
  • The glass door stays on while the pilot lights.

Light it

  1. Press the On/Off button on the remote.
  2. You'll hear a beep, then the igniter sparks. Once the pilot is lit and steady, the gas valve opens and the burner lights at full flame.
  3. Turn the flame down to a level you like with the remote.

In the ON or SMART thermostat modes it only lights if the set temperature is above the room temperature.

If the pilot doesn't light

The system locks out. Press On/Off to turn it off and reset it, wait five minutes for any gas to clear, then press On/Off again. Still won't run? Turn off the gas to the fireplace (see Heat & safety) and call your service technician or gas supplier.

If you smell gas: don't light any appliance, don't touch any electrical or light switch and don't use any phone in your building. Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow the gas supplier's instructions. If you can't reach your gas supplier, call the fire department.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The remote comes paired to your fireplace and runs on 3 AAA batteries. Stay within 20' of the fireplace. It beeps once each time a command is received; no beep, press again.

The four buttons

  • On/Off: turns the fireplace on (pilot first, then burners) and off.
  • Thermostat: picks OFF (Manual), ON (Normal Thermostat) or SMART.
  • Mode: steps through flame height, fan speed, accent light and rear burner.
  • Up / Down: changes the selected setting, or the set temperature.
OFF (Manual)runs whatever the room temperature; lights on Hi
ONturns itself on and off to hold your set temperature
SMARTholds the temperature by turning the flame up and down itself

Flame height and the accent light have six levels each; the fan has six speeds plus off. Switching the rear burner off cuts heat without changing the front flame. Pressing Down at flame level one turns the burners off.

Don't leave it burning unattended for long in Manual mode. The room can overheat. In Manual it shuts itself off after 24 hours of continuous use.

Child lock: press Mode and Up together; do the same to unlock. °F or °C: turn the fireplace off, then press Mode and Thermostat together.

curing.title: First fires: curing smoke and smell
curing.html:
A new fireplace has to cure. Materials left from manufacturing burn off and the paint hardens, so the first fires give off smoke and a strong smell. That's normal. Your installer should run the cure as the last install step, before the wall finish goes on.

The 3-step cure

  1. With the barrier screen (and any front or doors) on, set the thermostat to Manual (OFF), the flame to Hi and the fan to level 3. Run it at least 2 hours, then turn it off and let it cool. The fan keeps the smoke from staining the wall above.
  2. Manual mode, flame on Hi, fan off. Run it until the curing smell fades, then leave it on.
  3. Turn the fan down to level 1. If new smells appear, keep it running until they fade.
Smoke alarms: curing smoke will set them off. Open doors and windows; you can disable the alarms just for this step.

It's not unusual to need more than 10 hours on high before the smell fades. Slight odors can come back on later start-ups and fade with use. After three months or more unused, expect a burnt-dust smell at first, like your furnace in the fall.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass only once it has cooled to room temperature. You can clean the outside with a cleaner as needed. For the inside, take the glass frame off.

Removing the glass frame

  1. Use the glass latch tool that came with the fireplace. There are two spring latches on top: put the tool in the hole in each latch, pull it toward you and turn it 90° to release.
  2. Tip the top of the frame out about 8", lift it up about 1" and away.
  3. To refit it, set the two bottom tabs in their slots and center the frame. Tip it closed until the gasket touches, then re-hook the latches with the hooks facing down.

Each time the glass comes off, check that the gasket is in good shape and seals.

What to use

Kel Kem Polish Plus (part # 65-06-00455) or a comparable product. Never use oven cleaner or abrasive cleaners.

White film? The additives that give gas its smell can leave a white film on the glass. It comes off if you clean it promptly.
Never run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken. Replacing glass is a job for a licensed or qualified person.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI and CPI
modes.html:
The pilot is the small flame that lights the main burners. You choose how it behaves from the remote.

IPI (intermittent)the pilot lights only when the fireplace is called on, and goes out with the burners
CPI (continuous)the pilot stays lit; it shuts off after 7 days without use, and each use restarts the clock

Switching modes

  1. With the remote off, press Mode. The screen shows CPI or IPI.
  2. Press Up for CPI or Down for IPI.
  3. Press On/Off to start the fireplace.

A snowflake icon stays on the display the whole time CPI is on.

Why CPI in winter

A lit pilot keeps the chimney warm, so the fireplace drafts properly when it lights and is less likely to lock out. It also cuts condensation on the glass and stops cold drafts and heat loss through the glass door.

Note: the manual says CPI is required in winter when daily highs stay at 50°F or lower (p. 10), and calls it recommended when the average daily high falls below 50°F (p. 73).

wontstart.title: When it won't turn on
wontstart.html:
No beep from the remote

Check the 3 AAA batteries and stay within 20'. Still no beep? Pair the remote again:

  1. Flip the master switch up (on).
  2. Press and release the sync button, just above the master switch. The fireplace beeps three times.
  3. Within seven seconds, press the remote's on button. Four beeps mean it's paired.
Note: p. 69 puts the master and sync switches at the bottom left corner, in the left side air gap, then says the sync switch is above the master switch in the right-side air gap.

Remote beeps, but no fire

It may be in lockout. Turn the remote off. Then on, wait two seconds; off, wait two seconds; on, wait two seconds; and off. Now turn it on and start the fireplace, with the master switch on. Still nothing? Call your Mendota dealer.

No button works

The child lock may be on. Press Mode and Up together to turn it off.

It shut itself off

In Manual mode it turns off after 24 hours of continuous use. In the thermostat modes it turns off if it hears nothing from the remote for 60 minutes, for example when the remote is in another room or its batteries are very weak.

power.title: Power outages and batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on house power, but it can keep going through an outage on the backup battery pack that came with it (a holder for 4 AA batteries, 6V DC maximum).

During an outage

  1. Get the battery pack and its connecting harness from wherever you keep them.
  2. Plug the pack into the backup power inlet: the labeled wall plate your installer mounted to the left of the fireplace.
  3. Use the remote as usual.
Works on batterythe burner and flame height
Doesn't workthe fan and accent light

Keep the pack and harness somewhere safe and easy to find. Your installer should show you how to connect them.

Remote batteries

The remote takes 3 AAA batteries. Change them at least every 6 months, or sooner if you use the fireplace a lot. A battery icon appears on the remote's screen before they run out.

If a Versiheat or FlexHeat heat-transfer system was installed (for example, so a TV can hang above the fireplace), the fireplace can't be run during a power outage.

safety.title: Heat and safety around the fireplace
safety.html:
This is a heater. The glass, the wall above it and the hearth in front can get too hot to touch. The manual calls that normal when the clearances and finishing materials are right, so a few habits matter.

  • Barrier screen on, always. The supplied screen must be in place whenever the fireplace runs. If it's damaged, replace it with Mendota's barrier for this fireplace.
  • Keep a 60" zone. Furniture and other objects stay at least 60" in front of the barrier screen, and nothing goes on the front edge of the mantel.
  • Children and pets. Supervise them while it runs. If anyone at risk lives with you, add a safety gate too.
  • Bedrooms and studies. In an isolated room, use a thermostat mode, not Manual. Manual can make the room dangerously hot.
  • Gas only. Never burn wood or paper in it. If any part has been under water, don't use it: Mendota requires the whole fireplace to be replaced.

Shutting it down

In an emergency, flip the master switch down (off) and the main burners stop. To shut off the gas: turn the fireplace off with the remote, turn off CPI pilot mode, then close the manual gas valve inside the fireplace's left side (the left-side convection chamber). Put the tip of the glass latch tool in the hole in the valve bracket and turn it 90° counterclockwise until it stops. Also close the outside shutoff, if your installer fitted one. If service is to be performed, turn off all electric power to the fireplace.

service.title: Annual service and soot
service.html:
Your fireplace needs a service every year by a qualified installer, service agency or your gas supplier, in summer or early fall. Lint and dust build up, and insects can nest in the burner and orifice areas (the odorant added to natural gas attracts them).

What the yearly service covers

  • Cleaning lint and dust around the controls and blowers, and checking the wiring under the burner
  • Cleaning the pilot flame sensor and sparker rods; vacuuming the pilot assembly and burner ports
  • Checking the pilot and burner flames
  • Removing the logs and coals, cleaning off lint and carbon, and reinstalling them
  • Checking the glass gasket and the vent cap, and cleaning the glass

Your part

  • Check the outside vent cap regularly (the manual says monthly) for leaves, twigs or other debris.
  • Change the remote batteries at least every 6 months.
Soot means stop. A thin black film on the glass, soot patches bigger than 1"x1" on the logs, or soot on the house around the vent cap: turn the fireplace off and tell your Mendota dealer promptly. Small soot spots on the logs are acceptable.

Leave adjustments to the burner, pilot and logs to a qualified technician.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Mendota gives the original purchaser a limited lifetime warranty, as long as the fireplace stays where it was first installed. Coverage runs from the date Mendota invoiced your installing dealer, applies only to new units sold through an authorized Mendota dealer, and can't be transferred.

What's covered and for how long is set out in a table on this page of the manual. Check it there or ask your dealer.

Making a claim

Report the problem to your Mendota dealer within 30 days, with proof of purchase, the purchase date, model name and serial number. The serial number is on the listing label, which pulls out of the air gap below the glass frame. Your dealer submits the claim.

What voids it or isn't covered

  • Installation not done per the manual and codes, or without the required permits and inspections
  • Repairs by an unqualified technician, or skipped annual maintenance
  • Over-firing, water damage, misuse, or damage in transit
  • Discoloration, minor warping and noises from the steel expanding: these are normal

Replacement parts bought after coverage ends carry a 90-day warranty with a receipt (parts only, no labor).

This is a summary. The full conditions and exclusions are in the official PDF.

specInput.title: Input rates and orifices
specInput.html:
NG high / low fire44,000 / 14,100 BTUH
LP high / low fire44,000 / 18,600 BTUH
Orifices, NG#38 rear · #44 front
Orifices, LP#54 rear · #54 front
P.4 fireplace efficiency75%
Maker's website: CSA P.4.1 Efficiency 75%.

The same orifices are listed for [0-2000ft (610 m)] and [2000-4500ft (610-1370 m)]. The unit ships for natural gas; LP needs conversion kit # HA-110-00084. Above 7,500 ft, plan for gas input derating and contact Mendota Technical Service (venting too).

NG input check (p. 45): 30 minutes at maximum flame with all other appliances off; therms used × 100,000 × 2 must be at least 44,000 Btu/Hr.

Never over-fire or under-fire by changing orifice sizes or gas pressure. A "backyard" natural gas well needs gas analysis data sent to Mendota before first firing.

specGas.html:
NG supply7" W.C. [5.0" W.C. min., 11" W.C. max.]
LP supply11" W.C. [11" W.C. min., 13" W.C. max.]

Supply pressures are from the ratings page; manifold pressures are from the input-rate verification (p. 45). Two pressure taps on the main gas valve (left side of the firebox) read inlet and outlet pressure. The LP kit lists its motorized regulator # 907.012 as [10.0"-5.5" WC].

The soot troubleshooting chart uses the same outlet values: 3.5" W.C. Nat. Gas, 10" W.C. LP Gas (p. 77).

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Coaxial rigid pipe: 5" diameter exhaust and 8" diameter air inlet, with approved vent caps. Any UL Listed coaxial rigid 5"X8" components may be used, but one brand and series throughout. No "low profile" caps: they cause exhaust recirculation and ghosting flames. Same chart for NG and LP.

9" starter (minimum)12" max horizontal
12" starter3' 5"
2' starter12' 11"
3' starter22' 6"
4' – 12' starter32' (three 90° elbows allowed)
12' – 40' startervaries (see the chart drawing)
Max vertical run40'
Max vent system length44' (all straight sections added)
  • Starter under 4': use the chart, then subtract 3' for each 90° elbow after the first. Each horizontally positioned 45° elbow takes off 1½'. Two 45° elbows may replace one 90°.
  • Vertical terminations: up to four 90° elbows, the fourth pointing straight up to the cap, with at least 4 feet of vertical starter.
  • Horizontal runs level or rising ¼" per foot toward the cap, never downward. Support every 3 ft.
  • Twist-lock every joint so the system is leak-proof (DuraVent and American Metals: push together, then about ¼ turn clockwise).
Note: pp. 34, 46 and 54 say sealant isn't required at vent pipe joints (never silicone; stove gasket cement optional); p. 58 says to be sure 1000°F sealant is used in the inner pipe joints of all Simpson DuraVent pipe sections.

Three 90° elbows with a 3' starter: p. 56's worked example allows 16 ½' of horizontal run, and the three-elbow drawing on p. 59 refers you to the Master Venting Chart. The table on p. 59 (V, H1 + H2: 9' 11" for a 2' rise, 19' 6" for a 3' rise, 32' for 4' – 12') goes with that page's dual 90° elbow drawing.

Alternatives: a Mendota approved power vent (pp. 63-64) or masonry conversion kit # AA-11-03539 with a 5" flexible aluminum exhaust duct (p. 38).

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Unit to floor0"
Unit to enclosure sidewall1/2"
Unit to enclosure back wall1/2"
Unit bottom to enclosure ceiling54 in.
Unit bottom to room ceiling72 in.
Inner guide edge to adjacent sidewall16"
Vent pipe top / sides / bottom3" / 1" / 1"
Note: the ratings page gives body clearances of 1/2" from the unit to the enclosure sidewall and back wall (p. 15); "Clearance from Appliance" gives 5/8" from the side walls and 5/8" from the rear wall, plus 9-3/16" from the top surface (p. 22).

Side walls (p. 23): 16" from the side edge of the visible glass. Combustible walls, mantel legs and corbels must sit behind a 45-degree line from the glass side edges unless they are more than 16" away. A 20-gauge or heavier steel shield on 1" standoffs (open top and bottom, 12" larger than the heat source each way) cuts 16" by 66% to 5-3/8"; R-1 ceramic or mineral board cuts it 50% to 8".

Keep 3" above horizontal vent pipe and horizontal discharge elbows, including elbows enclosed in a wall, floor or ceiling. Never fill air spaces with insulation.

specMantel.title: Mantel and TV clearances
specMantel.html:
8" combustible mantel22" min. above the top of the heat outlet
Floor level to 8" mantel48-1/2"
Floor level to top air gap26-1/2"
Non-combustible mantelany height above the top opening

Mantels that protrude more than 8": use a rise and run of 1:1. The manual's example: a 12" mantel goes 12" x (1/1) + 14" = 26" above the convection air opening. A pre-existing combustible mantel must fall within the allowable mantel profile chart (Figure 3-12), which the manual shows as a drawing on this page.

TV above the fireplace (pp. 32-33)

  • A mantel at least 2" deeper than the TV and at least as wide, its top surface 12" min. above the top air gap. If the mantel is combustible, make certain the entire mantel meets the clearances to combustible mantels above.
  • A recessed cavity 6" taller and 6" wider than the TV, its bottom 16" min. above the top air gap, the TV recessed at least 2".
  • A heat transfer system (Cool Wall, two Versiheat fans, or FlexHeat) allows a TV 12" above the top air gap. The convection fans must be off; Versiheat/FlexHeat must run whenever the fireplace does, so no operation in a power outage.

Mendota leaves the TV decision and its temperature limits to the owner.

specHearth.title: Hearth pad
specHearth.html:
Fireplace on the floornon-combustible R-1 pad, 18" min. in front
Fireplace raisedreduce pad depth 2" per 1" raised
Raised 6" or moreno R-1 pad required (pp. 12, 25)
Under the fireplacewood or cement floor; no R-1 needed
Note: pp. 12 and 25 drop the hearth pad requirement when the fireplace is raised 6" or more; p. 17 drops it when the fireplace is raised more than 6".

Raising the fireplace only removes the R-1 requirement: the floor in front still gets up to 200 °F. With carpet, vinyl or laminate in front, Mendota recommends raising it at least 12". The pad's top surface can reach 250°F, which is normal.

The gap between the bottom of the fireplace and the bottom finishing guide must be covered: build the pad level with the guide, or raise the fireplace and cover the gap with non-combustible wall finish. Dimension "A" is 1 1/2" with the factory guide; with a thicker pad, raise the fireplace (a 4" pad means raising it 2 1/2"). The p. 12 warning lists the R-1 pad as "1-1/2" Thick Maximum".

Insulating boards (only under other non-combustible finish): Rescor 360 ceramic board 1/2", R 1.11; Fiberfrax Duraboard LD 1/2", R 1.10; Micore 160, 300, SB mineral fiber board 1/2". A 1" granite slab is only R .05.

Note: the manual gives the Micore R-value as 1.27 – 1.47 (p. 25) and 1.2 – 1.4 (p. 27).

specFrame.title: Rough framing and finishing
specFrame.html:
A · Enclosure framing width55"
B · Finished framing width48"
C · Framing height41"
D · Framing depth20"
E · Finish material thickness1"
F · Unit base to room ceiling72"
G · To side wall16"
H · Floor to 8" mantel48-1/2"
Net weight300 lbs. (team lift recommended)

These are minimums. Leave room on the left side for gas and electrical hookups; frame the front to the final 48" once the unit is in place. Recessed in a cavity deeper than 20"? Everything protruding past the fireplace face must be non-combustible.

Finishing (pp. 27-29)

  • Non-combustible zone: materials rated non-combustible per NFPA 220 or passing ASTM E 136. Paper-faced gypsum board (including Type X) and WonderBoard are not approved there.
  • Wall finish over the fireplace at least 1" deep is recommended (the finishing guide depth). Facing just outside the top convection air gap can reach 350°F.
  • Smooth walls: attach board to the wood framing and float it over the metal face, never screwed to it, with no seams above the fireplace.
  • Tile: unmodified dry-set mortar or hi-temp RTV silicone (48 hours cure), on non-combustible backer board in the non-combustible zone.
  • Stone: never a one-piece U-shaped marble, granite or natural stone facing (it cracks at the inner corners); heat-test polished stone samples first.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Supply120 VAC (minimum line voltage allowed 110 Volts AC)
Current1.5 Amps (p. 15) · 2 Amp (p. 39)
Backup6V DC power source
Blowersdual, standard: 190 CFM (in free air)
Note: the ratings page lists the current draw as 120 Volts AC, 1.5 Amps (p. 15); the electrical section says 120 VAC, 2 Amp power (p. 39).

The AC supply must be hot at all times, with no switch installed in it. It connects at the junction box on the left side through the strain relief. Ground per local codes, or NFPA 70 / CSA C22.1. Label all wires before disconnecting them when servicing controls; replacement wire must match the original insulation type and size.

In an outage the burner and flame height run on the DC battery pack; the fan and accent light don't.

conflicts.issue: Current draw: ratings page says 120 Volts AC, 1.5 Amps; electrical section says 120 VAC, 2 Amp power.
Body clearances: unit to enclosure sidewall/back wall 1/2 in. (ratings table) vs 5/8" from appliance side walls and rear wall ('Clearance from Appliance').
Master/sync switch location: 'bottom left corner of the fireplace in the left side air gap' vs sync switch 'above master switch in the right-side air gap' on the same page.
CPI in winter: 'required' when outside daily highs remain 50°F or lower (p. 10) vs 'recommended' when the average daily high falls below 50°F (p. 73); p. 87 says 'suggested'.

Vent joint sealant: not required, no silicone, stove gasket cement optional (pp. 34, 46, 54) vs 'Be sure 1000°F sealant is used in the inner pipe joints of all pipe sections manufactured by Simpson DuraVent' (p. 58).

Three 90° elbows with a 3' starter: p. 56 worked example gives 16 1/2' horizontal; the p. 59 table printed beside 'Three 90° Elbows' gives 19' 6" (H1 + H2). The p. 59 values equal the master chart minus 3' (one extra elbow) and the drawing on that page is labeled 'Dual 90° Elbows', so the table may belong to the dual-elbow drawing.
conflicts.reason: On p. 59 the V / H1 + H2 table sits in the left column with the 'Dual 90° Elbows' horizontal termination drawing (labeled V, H1, H2), and its values are the master chart's less 3' for the one added elbow (12' 11" to 9' 11", 22' 6" to 19' 6"). The 'Three 90° Elbows' caption in the right column (drawing labeled V1, H1, V2, H2) says to use the Master Venting Chart, which with p. 56's rule gives the worked example's 16 1/2'. Both read clearly once the table is tied to the dual-elbow drawing.

conflicts.issue: No hearth pad needed when raised '6" or higher/or more' (pp. 12, 25; p. 10 'at least 6"') vs 'raised more than 6"' (p. 17).
Micore mineral fiber board 1/2" R-value: 1.27 – 1.47 (p. 25) vs 1.2 – 1.4 (p. 27).
Natural gas air shutter opening: 0" to 1/8" (lighting checklist, p. 66) vs 1/8" open (air shutter section, p. 67).
Guide kit threshold for Grace/Willowbrook/Mission fronts: Recessed Mount kit required when wall finish exceeds 2 1/2" in depth vs Flush Mount kit usable with finish less than 3" thick.

review.notes: The manual is the FV42 FullView manual (Model No. AA-11-03792, 85-03-01109-T); it never uses the word 'Traditional'. The guide follows its log-set content (three log sets, p. 65; p. 41 notes Décor models don't use the Split Flow circuit). Catalog check: BTU (NG 44,000/14,100; LP 44,000/18,600) and 75% efficiency match p. 15; the catalog's efficiency basis 'P.4.1' is printed as 'P.4' in the manual. Overall unit dimensions appear only in Figure 3-4 (p. 17, no text), so catalog height/width/depth 41/48/20 can't be verified; they coincide with the framing table (framing height 41, finished framing width 48", framing depth 20"). Catalog view area 42 1/8 x 25 1/8 is not in the manual. Not transcribed (figure-only): overall dimensions (p. 17), allowable mantel profile chart (Fig. 3-12, p. 24), the master venting chart drawing (p. 55; only its printed V/H table is used), approved vent configuration drawings (p. 36), the warranty coverage table (p. 88; periods not in text), wiring diagram (p. 41), gas train and burner parts drawings (pp. 83-84). Minor wording differences shown or left out rather than flagged: thermostat-mode fan run-on 12-1/2 minutes (p. 70) vs 12 minutes (p. 87), not stated in the guide; listing label 'in the air gap below the firebox on the unit floor' on a chain (p. 13), 'below the bottom edge of the glass door frame' on a cable (p. 75), 'in the air gap on the side' (p. 45); 16" side-wall clearance measured from the 'inner guide edge' (p. 15) vs 'side edge of the visible glass' (p. 23), both shown; R-1 pad '1-1/2" Thick Maximum' (p. 12) vs a 4" pad with the unit raised (p. 26), both shown; vent length 'maximum 44'' (p. 55) vs 'less than 44 feet' (pp. 56, 58); p. 71 says the 'AUX On' function isn't used on this fireplace while p. 72 says aux switches optional heat transfer kits (guide omits AUX); p. 73 labels CPI 'Pilot on Demand' while pp. 10 and 69 call it continuous pilot; p. 76 gives house power as 110VAC vs 120 VAC elsewhere. The remote's beep signals (3 = ready to sync, 4 = accepted) aren't a published code table, so codes is empty.
